title: API shape sketch - inference config scratchpad
content:
Notes to self: quick sketch for a compact API + config shape we can test with the dedicated routing prototype. Keep this very small: fields that must exist for routing, caching, and graceful fallback.

High level goals:
- single request shape for hosted/dedicated/private that contains routing hints but is optional
- explicit fields so the control plane can compute cost estimates without full decode
- small, composable config blocks for batching, kv-cache, and model-fallback

Rough API request (proto/json sketch):

{
  "input": "<text or structured payload>",    // string or structured content, opaque to router
  "mode": "chat|completion|embed|rerank",
  "model_hint": "redwood-13b-v1|gptx-4-like",   // soft preference
  "latency_slo_ms": 100,                          // optional: guide routing decision
  "cost_sensitivity": "low|medium|high",       // affects fallback to quantized or smaller model
  "cache": {
    "prefix_key": "user:123:conv:456",        // for prefix caching, optional
    "max_ttl_secs": 300,
    "use_kv_cache": true
  },
  "batch": {
    "prefer_latency": true,                        // boolean preference, runtime may still batch
    "max_batch_ms": 20,
    "max_tokens_per_batch": 4096
  },
  "fallback_policy": {
    "allowed_variants": ["quantized", "cpu", "smaller-model"],
    "order": ["same-model-quant", "model-xxs", "region-fallback"]
  },
  "trace_id": "uuid-..."                          // for debug/tracing across control plane/runtime
}

Notes on fields:
- latency_slo_ms and cost_sensitivity are hints only; routing will combine with current load, model perf table and customer tier to pick a node.
- cache.prefix_key should be deterministic from user+prompt prefix; runtime may ignore if it can’t do safe prefix matching.
- We must be careful about semantics: cache/use_kv_cache true should not change generated tokens unless the cache is known-valid for the exact model/version. Mark as best-effort.

Example response (sketch):

{
  "id": "req-123",
  "chosen_model": "redwood-13b-v1-quant",
  "node_region": "us-west-2",
  "latency_ms": 78,
  "tokens_generated": 42,
  "billing_estimate": {
    "compute_units": 0.0023,
    "currency": "USD",
    "estimated_cost": "0.00055"
  },
  "warnings": ["served-from-kv-cache"]
}

Architecture ASCII (very rough):

Client -> API Gateway -> Control Plane Router -> [Policy Evaluator, Cost Estimator, Model Catalog] -> Node Selector -> Runtime Pool -> GPU Instance
                                     |
                                     +-> Telemetry / Trace collector

Routing decisions need inputs: request hints (latency, cost), catalog entries (model size, seq perf), current pool utilization, region constraints, customer reserved capacity.

Batching behavior (sketch):
- runtime keeps sliding window per model-variant+seq-dist.
- if request.prefers_latency => max wait = batch.max_batch_ms. But if cost_sensitivity == high, allow slightly longer wait to aggregate tokens.
- special case for streaming: start sending partial tokens once generation begins even if batch still active.

KV-cache semantics quick notes:
- store mapping: prefix_fingerprint -> KV state snapshot id
- on read: if model_version matches or is compatible (same arch + quantization profile) then apply. Otherwise return cache-miss.
- eviction: LRU + TTL from config.max_ttl_secs.
- privacy: if request has "sensitive": true flag, do not persist cache or write to centralized store.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Field name consistency: cost_sensitivity vs cost_priority vs price_tier? pick one.
- How to express hard vs soft region constraints (customer may require "must-run-in: eu-west-1"). Add explicit field region_constraints: { hard: [..], preferred: [..] }?
- Should the client be able to request a model variant by kernel/quant flags (e.g., "force_kernel: f16-ops")? danger: leaks runtime knobs to users. Maybe keep as internal hint only.
- Streaming API shape: do we change request shape or keep same and add headers? prefer single JSON over header proliferation.

Mini test plan (what to prototype):
- implement router that honors latency_slo_ms and cost_sensitivity for a single model family.
- simulate requests with prefix cache hits/misses and measure end-to-end latency distribution with/without batching.
- quick experiment: allow fallback to quantized variant when compute_util > 80% and compare quality drop on small eval set.

Random scribbles: 
- For SDK convenience, expose a small builder: Request().with_model_hint('r13b').with_latency_slo(150).with_cache_prefix('u:1:c:3')
- Make sure trace_id is sampled into dataplane logs and appears in console traces for debugging.

UX note: default client libs should not expose low-level kernel selection. Instead provide profiles: "high_quality" (no quant), "balanced" (quantize if needed), "cheap" (aggressive quant + smaller models).

End of scratchpad. Keep as living doc — copy into a proper PR/rfc once we have early numbers from simulation.
